implementation_constraints.detail: All three optional inputs must be present and nonempty or all absent. No runtime/request/env READY authority. Disabled mode must produce no activation ldflags/helper artifact and record disabled status; existing Host defaults stay empty/closed. Only Core receives the two fixed fully qualified -X symbols.

Freeze one CLI digest syntax. Recommended raw64 lowercase hex; reject whitespace/prefix/uppercase alternatives unless deliberately specified. The actual linked Host helper value must be exactly sha256:<64 lowercase hex>, because codexBuildDigest requires that form. Bind expected raw digest, actual source/copy digest and exact linked value in manifest.

Validate original absolute Windows spelling, existing ordinary directory root and regular .exe helper, and every existing ancestor's reparse bit before resolve; reject alias spellings, junction/symlink/reparse, drive-relative paths, UNC/device paths, ADS, NUL/control and Host-forbidden semicolon. Do not silently canonicalize an alias and accept it. Do not create or change external root/S. If root does not yet exist, fail and let a separate Root preparation scope establish it. S may be derived for manifest; do not claim its existence/identity was checked unless actually checked.

Pass one structured argv list with shell=False; Go -ldflags still performs its own tokenization. Either use a source-verified Go quoting rule or explicitly reject unsupported whitespace/quote characters for root while retaining required Unicode support. A root string must never introduce a third linker option. Set GOFLAGS empty in the shared child environment before all Go list/build and nested builder calls; do not merely remove it from logs. Tests assert exact Core argv, two symbol assignments, verifier/other commands unmodified, and attempted quote/whitespace injection rejection.

Treat helper as prebuilt expected-hash input: check predeclared digest and size before build/copy, copy once to a fixed bundle-relative path under the fresh controlled output, then verify source and destination again before successful manifest/receipt. Validate output target ancestry and reject collisions/drift; retain failure artifacts. No writes to external helper source/root/S and no execution of the helper or any bundled executable.

Snapshot cmd/researchos-qualification-helper/ specifically plus existing internal/qualificationprobe sources, and admit the new pure-test file to snapshot scope. Current helper source hashes alone do not prove a supplied binary was built from them. Label supplied helper as prebuilt/hash-bound; Root must bind its original reviewed build receipt/compiled closure and show source compatibility. Do not relabel a fresh go-list closure as the prebuilt binary's historical build closure. Existing Core/verifier compiled closure remains separate.

Manifest records disabled/enabled, exact root and derived S with validation status, helper input path/size/expected and actual hash, fixed bundle path/copied hash, exact two linker values and actual Core build argv, resulting Core hash, snapshot and compiled-closure provenance, exact file inventory, BUILT_NOT_NATIVE_TESTED and acceptance0. A build pin may enable Host construction only after separately prepared runtime prerequisites; it is not permission to run qualification or a model.

review_limits: Read-only review of proposal plus current build-development.py and Host symbol parser. Helper-only build01 result/hash/size was supplied by Root and not independently re-audited here.
No implementation reviewed or source acceptance granted yet. Author must freeze exact3 changes for independent review; Root alone registers pure tests/full build under original f13.
Existing build script itself launches compiler and existing client/Mu build tools only in future registered build; this review executed none of them.
No additional source path, Host/runtime edit, packaging execution, external-directory write or actual qualification scope is authorized by this verdict.

diagnostic_events.detail: Exact3 build-only scope is sufficient with fixed linker/hash/path/provenance rules above. Implementation and runtime qualification remain separately gated.
